text:
**I’d stay on Monzo Free unless a paid plan replaces something you already buy.** Perks is the easiest to justify if you use its subscriptions or regularly go to Vue. Extra is mainly about budgeting convenience; Max is mainly an insurance decision. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/current-account/plans))

| UK plan | Cost as of November 2026 | When I’d choose it |
|---|---:|---|
| **Extra** | **£3/month (£36/year)** | If you’d use virtual cards, custom spending categories or the ability to see multiple bank accounts in Monzo every week. If you only want to link **one** other account, Free already does that. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/current-account/plans)) |
| **Perks** | **£9/month (£108/year)** | If the eligible annual Railcard, monthly Vue ticket, weekly Greggs treat, Uber One or YouTube Premium Lite replace at least £9 of typical monthly spending between them. It also includes Extra. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/monzo-max/monzo-plan-price-change)) |
| **Max** | **£19/month (£228/year)** | If you already want Perks, the question is whether worldwide travel insurance, phone insurance and UK/Europe breakdown cover are worth **another £120/year**. If you don’t value Perks, compare standalone cover against the **full £228** instead. Family cover costs **£23/month (£276/year)**. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/current-account/max?utm_source=openai)) |

**A quick Perks break-even test:** If you’d otherwise buy a **£35 annual Railcard**, that leaves **£73 a year**, or **£6.08 a month**, to recover. If you already go to Vue monthly and normally pay more than £6.08 per ticket, those two benefits alone cover the plan. Count the £35 you avoid paying for the Railcard, *not* the train-fare discounts you’d get either way. Equally, a Greggs coffee you’d never otherwise buy isn’t a cash saving. ([nationalrail.co.uk](https://www.nationalrail.co.uk/railcards/?utm_source=openai))

**Before choosing Max**, check whether you already have breakdown or phone cover, and whether the travel policy covers your trips and medical circumstances. Max has a **three-month minimum term**. And on either Perks or Max, claiming the Railcard then cancelling early can trigger a fee. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/legal/max/terms-and-conditions?utm_source=openai))
